facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
On 6 May 2012 the applicant took part in the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it transpired that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue.
The barriers installed by the police at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012 allegedly restricted the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, a police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police began to disperse the participants of the meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protestors from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected acts of mass disorder under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 6 May 2012 the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation opened criminal proceedings to investigate suspected violence against the police under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation.

On 18 May 2012 the criminal case file was transferred from the Moscow city department of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation to the headquarters of the Investigative Committee of the Russian Federation for further investigation.
On 9 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having participated in acts of mass disorder during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 9 June 2012 the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having used violence against the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 9 June 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow ordered the applicant's pre-trial detention until 9 August 2012.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow's detention order of 9 June 2012 referred to the gravity of the charges against the applicant.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow's detention order of 9 June 2012 referred to information about the applicant's personality.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow noted in its detention order of 9 June 2012 that the applicant's father was a Ukrainian national living in Ukraine.
The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow noted in its detention order of 9 June 2012 that the applicant might flee to Ukraine to avoid the investigation and trial.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow concluded in its detention order of 9 June 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant, if at liberty, was likely to continue his criminal activity.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow concluded in its detention order of 9 June 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant, if at liberty, was likely to influence witnesses.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow concluded in its detention order of 9 June 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant, if at liberty, was likely to destroy evidence.

The Basmannyy District Court of Moscow concluded in its detention order of 9 June 2012 that the circumstances gave sufficient reasons to believe that the applicant, if at liberty, was likely to otherwise obstruct the investigation of the criminal case, which was at an initial stage.
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (participation in acts of mass disorder accompanied by violence).
On 18 June 2012 charges were brought against the applicant under Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation (use of violence against a public official).
On 11 July 2012 the Moscow City Court upheld the detention order of 9 June 2012 issued by the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow.
On 7 August 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow examined an investigator's request for an extension of the applicant's pre-trial detention.
At the hearing on 7 August 2012, the applicant requested that an alternative preventive measure be applied pending trial, such as house arrest.
At the hearing on 7 August 2012, the applicant requested that an alternative preventive measure be applied pending trial, such as a written undertaking not to leave a specified place.

On 7 August 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow found that the circumstances that had justified the detention order had not changed and extended the applicant's detention until 6 November 2012.
On 5 September 2012 the Moscow City Court upheld the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow's decision of 7 August 2012 extending the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 November 2012.
On 2 November 2012 the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow authorised a further extension of the applicant's detention until 6 March 2013.

In its decision of 2 November 2012, the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow reiterated the grounds given in the previous extension orders and stated that the circumstances justifying the detention order had not changed.
On 3 December 2012 the Moscow City Court upheld the Basmannyy District Court of Moscow's decision of 2 November 2012 extending the applicant's pre-trial detention until 6 March 2013.
On 21 November 2012 the charges against the applicant were reformulated.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had shouted insulting slogans during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had used metal barriers to obstruct the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had at least three times thrown stones and pieces of tarmac at police officers during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had once punched a policeman during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had grabbed a police officer's uniform during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
The reformulated charges of 21 November 2012 additionally stated that the applicant had snatched a protection helmet from a police officer's hands during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
On 29 November 2012 Police Officer P. identified the applicant during an identification parade as a participant in the mass disorder at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

On 29 November 2012 Police Officer P. identified the applicant during an identification parade as the person who had twice thrown pieces of tarmac at the police during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.

On 29 November 2012 Police Officer P. identified the applicant during an identification parade as the person who had tried to snatch a protection helmet from a policeman's hands during the demonstration of 6 May 2012.
Police Officer P. specified during the identification parade on 29 November 2012 that he had not seen whether the applicant had in fact succeeded in snatching the helmet or not.

On 7 December 2012 the investigator of the Zamoskvoretskiy Inter-district Investigation Committee of Moscow refused to open a criminal case into allegations made by the applicant that he had been subjected to ill-treatment by the police during his arrest.

The investigator of the Zamoskvoretskiy Inter-district Investigation Committee of Moscow considered on 7 December 2012 that the use of force by the police had been justified by the behaviour of the protesters, including the applicant, who had thrown various objects at the police officers.

At the hearing on 19 November 2013, the applicant presented a personal guarantee from a member of the State Duma in support of an undertaking by him to appear before the investigating authorities and the courts for the examination of his case.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow did not consider the personal guarantee from a member of the State Duma presented by the applicant at the hearing on 19 November 2013.

On 19 November 2013 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow ordered that the applicant and his co-defendants be detained until 24 February 2014 on the grounds of gravity of the charges and the nature of the offences imputable to them.

Article 212 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the organisation of mass disorder, accompanied by violence, riots, arson, destruction of property, the use of firearms, explosives and explosive devices, as well as armed resistance to a public official, shall be punishable by four to ten years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 2 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that participation in the types of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1 shall be punishable by three to eight years' deprivation of liberty.

Article 212 § 3 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the instigation of mass disorder provided for by Article 212 § 1, or the instigation of participation in such acts, or the instigation of violence against citizens, shall be punishable by a restriction of liberty for up to two years, or community service for up to two years, or deprivation of liberty for the same term.

Article 318 § 1 of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation provides that the use of violence which does not endanger life or health, or the threat to use such violence against a public official or his relatives in connection with the performance of his or her duties, shall be punishable by a fine of up to 200,000 roubles or an equivalent of the convicted person's wages for 18 months, or community service for up to five years, or up to five years' deprivation of liberty.
